title: Allergies or Cold Decision Guide
source_title: Bogan Weekly News | Smore Newsletters for Education
summary: The school nurse provides a visual flowchart to help determine whether symptoms indicate allergies or a cold. Key differences: **allergies** typically cause itchy eyes/nose/throat, clear mucus, and symptoms that occur seasonally or persist for extended periods; **colds** typically cause green/yellow mucus, body discomfort, fever, and symptoms that come on fast and taper off quickly. **Call your doctor if** symptoms last longer than two weeks, worsen or new symptoms develop, you have a sore throat or fever higher than 100 degrees for longer than three days, or you experience intense chest pain and shortness of breath.

title: Allergies or Cold: Know the Difference
source_title: Bogan Weekly News | Smore Newsletters for Education
summary:
The school nurse provides a diagnostic flowchart to help distinguish between allergies and a cold. Key differentiators include:
- **Mucus color**: Clear mucus suggests allergies; green or yellow suggests a cold
- **Symptom duration**: Seasonal or extended symptoms indicate allergies; quick onset and resolution suggests a cold
- **Itchiness**: Itchy eyes, nose, and throat are more common with allergies
- **Fever**: Having a fever points toward a cold rather than allergies

**Call your doctor if** symptoms last longer than two weeks, worsen, include sore throat/fever over 100°F for more than three days, or involve intense chest pain and shortness of breath.

title: Understanding Decoding: Reading Skills Resources for Parents
source_title: Bogan Weekly News | Smore Newsletters for Education

blocks.content: What does decoding mean? A simple definition for decoding is recognizing letter sounds or patterns and blending them together to translate a written word into speech. Decoding is a foundational reading skill (phonics) that must be developed to begin successful reading with fluency. This process begins with students recognizing their letters and sounds then blending the sounds to speak the word, i.e., /c/ - /a/ - /t/ becomes cat.Here is an example of what happens when a student decodes a word:Recognizing letters and letter patterns (like b, sh, igh)Knowing the sounds they makeBlending those sounds together to read a wordActivities: Reading Rockets is a reputable research-based website for all things reading; and below are age-specific resources for decoding activities.Kindergarten: https://www.readingrockets.org/literacy-home/reading-101Kindergartener phonics and decoding activitiesFirst Grade:https://www.readingrockets.org/literacy-home/reading-101-guide-parents/your-first-grader/phonics-and-decoding-activitiesSecond Grade:https://www.readingrockets.org/literacy-home/reading-101-guide-parents/your-second-grader/phonics-and-decoding-activitiesThird Grade:Here is a video showing how a 3rd grade student uses syllables to decode longer words more easily.

summary:
**Decoding** is the foundational reading skill of recognizing letter sounds and blending them together to read words (e.g., /c/ - /a/ - /t/ = cat). Reading Rockets provides age-specific activities for parents to support decoding practice:
- **Kindergarten**: [Phonics and decoding activities](https://www.readingrockets.org/literacy-home/reading-101)
- **First Grade**: [Phonics and decoding activities](https://www.readingrockets.org/literacy-home/reading-101-guide-parents/your-first-grader/phonics-and-decoding-activities)
- **Second Grade**: [Phonics and decoding activities](https://www.readingrockets.org/literacy-home/reading-101-guide-parents/your-second-grader/phonics-and-decoding-activities)
- **Third Grade**: Video showing how students use syllables to decode longer words
